fields.meta_description: Build an identity verification form that takes photo ID uploads and sends each case to a reviewer on your team.
fields.hero_description: An identity verification form pairs a person's details with a photo of their ID so your team can confirm who they are. Emergent builds the form and the review queue.
fields.features_heading: Every Upload Lands in a Review Queue
fields.features_subheading: Most identity verification forms are PDFs sent back by mail. Emergent's version takes the photos and queues each case for a reviewer.
fields.feature_1:
Front and back of the ID

Asks for the front and the back of a photo ID as two separate uploads, with a preview before submit. Files go to storage your organization owns, next to the person's record.
fields.feature_2:
Document rules you set

Lets the person pick one photo ID or two supporting documents, then shows only the upload slots that choice needs. Change the accepted list by prompt when policy changes.
fields.feature_3:
A reviewer makes every call

Places each submission in a queue beside the details the person typed. A reviewer compares the two side by side, then approves the case or sends it back with a reason attached.
fields.feature_4:
Expiry dates checked on entry

Stops the form when the expiry date someone types has already passed, before the case reaches your team. IDs that lapse within a month can be flagged for a closer look.
fields.feature_5:
Sensitive fields kept narrow

Shows Social Security numbers and ID images only to the reviewer role you name. Files are deleted on the schedule your retention policy sets, and the record keeps the decision.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take in-house

Exports the full codebase to your GitHub repository. Your engineers can host it, connect it to the account system you already run, or ask Emergent to build that connection.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Teams That Check ID Remotely
fields.tab_content_1:
Lights on once the license and lease agree

Power companies open accounts for people they never meet. A new Northwind Power customer uploads both sides of her driver's license and a signed lease from her phone. Sam Patel on the accounts team checks that the name and service address match, marks her verified at 10:42 AM, and her start date is booked.
fields.tab_content_2:
Aid held for 28 students who have not verified

Aid offices work to disbursement dates. Lakeside College selected 140 students for an identity check this term, and a counselor has approved the photo ID and signed statement for 112 of the 140. The other 28 stay on hold, and each gets an email reminder every 5 days until their documents arrive.
fields.tab_content_3:
Notarized by mail, checked by the clerk in one pass

Some requesters cannot come to the counter. Riverbend County's records office sends them a prefilled page with a notary section to sign in front of a notary. The requester uploads the scan, and the clerk checks the notary seal and a name that matches the request before releasing the certified copy.
fields.tab_content_4:
Expired IDs bounce back ahead of any payout

Marketplaces pay sellers they know only by email. Initech Market's KYC review shows 20 new sellers this week, and 3 entered an ID expiry date that has already passed. Each of those 3 shops gets a re-upload request by email, and payout setup waits until a reviewer approves the replacement ID.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Identity Verification Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps for the team that receives the form: what to ask, which documents count and who decides.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask only for what you will compare
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the rule before you add a single field. Many offices accept one unexpired photo ID, or a pair of supporting documents such as a utility bill and a bank statement. Both the form and the reviewer follow that rule, down to the wording of a rejection email.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Collect the details your process checks against the ID, usually the legal name and date of birth. Leave out fields no reviewer looks at, because every extra answer is personal data you have to store and later delete.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Request each side of the ID as its own upload, in color, with all four corners in the frame. Put an example of a photo that passes on the form itself. A blurry or cropped image means a second round trip for everyone.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Have the person type the ID's expiry date and stop the form if that date has passed. Catching an expired license at the form saves a reviewer from opening a case that can only end in a request for a new upload.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Give the decision to a person
fields.howto_step_5_des: Route each submission to a named reviewer, who compares the typed details with the images and marks the case verified or returned. Record who decided and when. Emergent builds the queue; it does not judge whether a document is genuine.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Offer a path without a smartphone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Some people have no phone camera or no current photo ID. Offer a printable page with a notary section, or an appointment at your office, and track those cases in the same queue as the online submissions.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Limit access and delete on schedule
fields.howto_step_7_des: Show ID images and Social Security numbers only to the reviewer role. Agree a retention period with your counsel, then delete the files when it ends and keep only the decision and who made it.

plan.angle: The top results are one organization's form each (an airline, a state health exchange, a utility, a university aid office, a public health district's notary page) plus one template download and Login.gov. Every one is a PDF or a page that ends with mail it in or email it. Searchers need to know which documents count and how the check works. This page answers that with sourced facts (I-9 lists, Social Security's rules), then builds the part a PDF cannot: ID uploads front and back, a reviewer queue where a person makes the call, expiry checks, a notarized mail-in path and re-upload requests. It never claims automated or biometric verification.

claims_to_source: For Form I-9, an employee shows one List A document, or one List B document (identity) plus one List C document (employment authorization); List B includes a state driver's license or ID card and List C includes an unrestricted Social Security card
Social Security accepts a U.S. driver's license, a state-issued non-driver ID card or a U.S. passport as proof of identity

People who cannot use a personal my Social Security account prove identity at an office only for retirement, survivors or auxiliary claims; irregular phone claims are sent to in-person identity proofing
People who cannot create a personal my Social Security account can get help at a local Social Security office, with an appointment
A personal my Social Security account is reached through Login.gov or ID.me
Login.gov identity verification asks for a driver's license, state ID or passport, a Social Security number and a U.S. phone number or mailing address
Login.gov lets people finish identity verification in person at a participating Post Office after starting online, with an unexpired driver's license or state ID
In California, a notary takes an acknowledgment only with satisfactory evidence that the signer is the person described in the document
